comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body:
A concrete instance of the cost, measured today while building a Matter controller in a Muster pane.

**Local Network is a fourth kind of protected request, and it fails worse than the three the description lists.** A folder or camera denial is recognizable as a denial. This one surfaces as a network error: every mDNS advertisement returns `OS Error 0x02000041: No route to host` (EHOSTUNREACH) on the multicast send, and nothing anywhere says "permission". Interfaces, routing and `IP_MULTICAST_IF` all got investigated first, because that is what the error points at.

**The obvious sanity check confirms the wrong thing.** `dns-sd -B _matter._tcp local.` keeps working throughout, because it asks mDNSResponder rather than sending multicast itself. So "mDNS works fine on this machine" is true, and says nothing about whether your own process can do it.

Confirmed in both directions rather than inferred. In a pane, every advertisement fails. Same binary, same flags, launched by hand from a GUI terminal: clean startup, no advertisement errors, server reachable and answering. The pane was the post-relaunch case - `herdr server` at pid 1598 with PPID 1, orphaned to launchd and older than the running muster at pid 29467, the chain reading `zsh <- claude <- rad <- -zsh <- herdr server` with no app anywhere in it.

None of this changes the options on the card. It raises what the status quo costs. A permission that fails as a routing error is one the person answering never gets asked about, so the pane case is not "the prompt names something else" but "no prompt at all, and an error pointing somewhere unrelated".

Independently of which way this goes: `observations/macos-26.4.1.md` names folder, camera and AppleScript. Local Network is worth adding there precisely because its failure is unrecognizable as a permission problem.

comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body:
**Decided: Launch Services starts it, from a helper bundle Muster ships inside its own. launchd is rejected.** Measured with all four arrangements side by side; `tools/tcc-probe` now records them and `docs/observations/macos-26.4.1.md` sections 1 and 8 read off the transcript.

**What the measurement says.** Responsibility is inherited from the spawning process, not read off the executable. So:

- a bare binary spawned by the app (today) - panes charged to Muster, then to themselves
- a *bundle's executable* spawned by the app - identical for panes. The daemon keeps its bundle name afterwards; its panes are still their own nameless subjects. This was the cheapest thing that could have worked and it does not.
- the same bundle opened through Launch Services - daemon is its own responsible process from its first instant, and every pane it ever makes is charged to it, before the app exits, after it, and for panes made later. One subject, permanently, with a bundle behind it.
- a bare binary under a launchd job - same consistency, and `prompts-say=nothing - no bundle`.

**So the card's first bullet resolves rather than trading off.** launchd buys consistency at the cost of any name at all, and the cost is worse than the card assumed: macOS reads a usage string from the responsible process's bundle, and a protected request with no declared string is a kill rather than a worse prompt. `dev` declares nineteen of them and a bare daemon can read none. Launch Services buys the same consistency and keeps them.

Also against launchd, and not on the card: installing a LaunchAgent puts an entry in Login Items & Extensions and macOS announces it. Observed while probing - "probe-bare can run in the background" - on a project whose answer to "how do I get herdr" is "you don't".

**Third option, considered and rejected as the card asked.** Re-exec'ing an orphaned daemon on relaunch would give consistent attribution by making the daemon young again, and costs every live process: a daemon restart keeps the pane tree, pane ids and cwds, and loses every terminal id, all scrollback and every running agent (`observations/herdr-0.8.0.md` section 12). That is what the durability guarantee exists to prevent.

**SSH is untouched**, as the card said it would be. A remote daemon has no TCC subject here; `remote::start` still uses `nohup`.

**Local Network is now in the observation file** as a fourth kind of protected request, with the control that makes it recognizable: same process, same instant, the datagram to the LAN gateway goes and the one to the mDNS group does not, so routing is not what refused it. `tools/tcc-probe/probe --here` establishes that in five seconds.

**One trap worth recording for whoever touches this next.** `open` hands the app its own environment and applies `--env` on top, so unlike the spawn's `env_clear` it carries whatever launched Muster. First cut gave the daemon 97 variables including the launching agent's `CLAUDECODE` and a `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH` pointing at another daemon, which herdr obeys over everything else - the bug a_28YgGqYq7 fixed, arriving again by a different door, and invisible because the window opens and works. `env_clear` on `open` itself is the fix; the daemon then holds fifteen variables and none of them are the launching session's.

Verified end to end on a real bundle: daemon started from `Muster.app/Contents/Library/MusterSessions.app` with ppid=1, a program in one of its panes reporting `responsible=` that daemon.

creator: Alexander Terp
description:
macOS charges a protected request - a folder, the camera, AppleScript - to the responsible process, and for a pane's program that is whichever Muster started its daemon. Measured on 26.4.1 and written up in `docs/observations/macos-26.4.1.md`: it holds while that Muster is alive, and the moment it exits every surviving pane becomes its own responsible process. A later Muster cannot adopt them - responsibility is fixed when a process is spawned and nothing lets an app claim a chain it did not start.

So today a permission behaves one way before the first relaunch and another way after it, under two different names, and neither prompt says which case you are in. That is the part worth fixing; the panes still work.

A daemon started by launchd would be its own responsible process from the first moment, so every pane it ever makes is attributed the same way whether or not a Muster is running. That is consistency rather than a fix: prompts would name the daemon rather than Muster, and a grant to Muster.app would stop covering panes at all.

What it costs is the thing that makes `architecture.md`'s "Muster ships its daemon and talks to no other" simple: the daemon stops being the app's own child, so which daemon a window is attached to becomes a question about an installed job rather than about a process Muster started. It also adds something somebody has to install, on a project whose current answer to "how do I get herdr" is "you don't".

Worth deciding rather than defaulting:

- **Whether consistency is worth losing Muster's own name on the prompt.** A prompt reading `herdr` explains less to the person answering it than one reading Muster, even if it is the same answer every time.
- **Whether a third option exists.** Muster could re-exec the daemon on a relaunch it finds orphaned, trading the surviving processes for consistent attribution - which is the one thing the durability guarantee exists to prevent, so probably not, but it should be written down as considered.
- **What it does to the SSH case.** A remote daemon is already outside all of this, so any answer here is about the local one only.

Comes out of a_28Tme94w3, which fixed the wording of the prompts and left this decision open.
title: 🔐 Should launchd start the daemon, so permissions behave the same every launch?
